text:
alexa: VendorCloud (acct 6059) ping — April invoice discrepancy. They say portal shows $4,500.00 but card charge is $45.00 and they have two PDFs with same invoice id. One PDF lists hourly usage, the other collapses all usage into a single line with a huge multiplier.
marcus: that sounds like a CSV-parsing bug that exploded a quantity column. @billing-bot can you pull run 2026-04-30-6059 and the dispatched PDFs?
billing-bot: invoice-run id=2026-04-30-6059 started 2026-04-30T23:50Z finished 2026-05-01T00:02Z. Status: completed with errors. Errors: [csv_parse:col_shift], [pdf_dispatch:duplicate_send]. Generated PDFs: invoice_2026-04-30-6059_v1.pdf (total 45.00), invoice_2026-04-30-6059_v2.pdf (total 4500.00).
julia: csv_parse:col_shift usually means a malformed usage export where an extra comma in a description shifted the quantity into price or qty fields. We recently added free-text notes to usage lines; could be the culprit.
alexa: customer says the card shows $45.00 (correct) but their accounting sees the $4,500 doc and is raising a dispute unless we resend corrected paperwork. They want a signed correction and an explanation.
marcus: short remit: 1) place account on billing-hold; 2) identify which PDF was attached to the payment capture and match that to DB; 3) re-generate canonical invoice from sanitized CSV and issue correction; 4) credit/void the erroneous invoice if it was marked published.
billing-bot: payment capture trace: pay_9b2c, amount_cents=4500.00 -> actually payment gateway normalized to 4500 cents = $45.00 and attached PDF invoice_2026-04-30-6059_v1.pdf. Database invoice record overwritten later by v2 publish.
julia: confirms: sanitized CSV dry-run shows a single-line summary total of 4500 cents and line items sum to 4500 cents. The v2 PDF error came from a codepath that concatenates description fields with commas, which then got consumed by naive CSV writer when re-ingesting.
alexa: customer ETA: wants corrected invoice within 4 hours. can finance expedite a void+correction?
finance-bot: created provisional credit memo CM-2026-0999 for acct 6059 to cover any duplicate charge if needed. Status: pending-approval. Approver: marcus.
marcus: approved. Julia, can you patch the CSV writer to escape commas in free-text and add a validation step that totals must equal payment capture if present?
julia: will push PR for CSV escaping and validation, and run a targeted regen job in dry-run. posting CSV here in 15m.
billing-bot: regen dry-run 2026-04-30-6059-rr completed: canonical invoice total=45.00, line items attached. Publish flag=false.
alexa: looks good. next: void the bad invoice record in portal (the 4500.00 one) and issue INV-2026-0430-CORR matching the captured payment. Also include short note: "Formatting error in usage export caused a misformatted invoice; we have voided the incorrect document and issued a corrected invoice."
marcus: ensure webhook dispatch only sends the corrected PDF once. disable retries for this invoice id.
finance-bot: actioned: INV-2026-0430 voided, INV-2026-0430-CORR created and published, CM-2026-0999 placed on account but will be voided if not needed. Customer portal updated and payment match confirmed.
julia: pushed hotfix to CSV writer and added unit test to prevent unescaped commas in description fields. Also added a pre-publish check that invoice total equals payment capture when capture exists.
alexa: vendor confirmed receipt of corrected invoice and portal update. they thanked us and asked for a short note for their records; i'll send the standard two-line explanation.
marcus: root cause summary: free-text in usage export introduced unescaped commas -> CSV reimport produced col_shift -> regen published different totals. Fix: escape on export, validation before publish, and idempotent PDF dispatch.
vendor-ops: filing a vendor-facing advisory to remind partners about quoting commas in free-text fields.
alexa: closing the loop. customer dispute dropped. Thanks team.
